boundary: chip_or_module (NVML per-GPU counter; excludes host CPU/DRAM and datacenter PUE)
method: ignore_eos fixed-length decode; warm-up generation discarded; median of repeats
_why_this_matters: L4 IS inside the fog hardware_class layer_energy.yaml declares (T4/L4/A30/A2/A16/L40S).
The curve this would replace is transcribed from an RTX 4090, which is NOT in that
class, and is measured at NODE boundary (CPU+GPU+DRAM) rather than the chip boundary
the file declares as its base. So even three points are an evidence upgrade in kind,
not just in count -- but they are three points, and the interesting part of the curve
(where batching saturates) starts past batch=8 and was not reached.
_observation: Over batches 1-4 the scaling is almost exactly linear: package power pins at 72 W while
throughput doubles with each batch doubling, so J/token halves (2.443 -> 1.234 -> 0.623).
That is the memory-bound regime -- the GPU is idle-waiting on weight loads, so extra
concurrent sequences ride along nearly free. The saturation knee, where power finally
rises and J/token stops halving, is what batches 8-32 were meant to find.
